quickAnswer: Westborough leans on electric heat and larger buildings: 26.8% of homes heat with electricity (3rd highest of the 50 towns we serve), 42.7% sit in multi-unit buildings and 39.1% of households rent. Oil heats only 20.0%, and utility gas leads at 48.5%.
body: ## Where electric heat and apartments set the agenda

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 8,552 housing units in Westborough, and three of its numbers stand out among the 50 towns we serve. Electricity heats 2,133 occupied homes (26.8%), the 3rd-highest share. Multi-unit buildings hold 3,651 homes (42.7%), also 3rd. And 3,112 households rent (39.1%), 4th. Single-family detached houses are only 49.3% of the stock, 48th of 50.

With 42.7% of homes in multi-unit buildings, shared systems and shared decisions are part of the picture. Where a household heats with electricity, the efficiency of the equipment shows up directly on its electric bill.
## Electric heat: baseboard, plug-in and heat pump

The 26.8% is far above the 10.1% of the middle town. Electric heat includes baseboard, electric furnaces and heat pumps, and the census does not say which. The first two use a lot of electricity for each unit of heat. A cold-climate heat pump can produce the same warmth with less electricity. Utility gas still leads at 3,863 homes (48.5%), and oil heats 1,589 (20.0%), a share the town ranks 44th for.

A failed gas boiler in Westborough does not automatically mean another gas boiler. We check what the building has and whether gas is piped to it. In a multi-unit building, the owner may also weigh one shared system against separate ones for each apartment.
## Rentals, vacancies and a median build year of 1976

The median home was built in 1976, and 4,864 homes (56.9%) predate 1980. The town also has 590 vacant units, a 6.9% vacancy rate that ranks 3rd of 50, compared with 3.6% for the middle town. Vacant buildings can still need some heat in winter to protect pipes. The town also ranks 10th of 50 for homes built since 2010, against 8.4% for the middle town, so newer construction sits alongside the older stock.

Massachusetts sets minimum temperatures for rented homes during the heating season, roughly mid-September to mid-June: at least 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight. Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord pays for heat. General information, not legal advice.
## A crossroads town with a long building record

Westborough has been a crossroads since long before recorded time, and it was incorporated on November 18, 1717 as the hundredth town in Massachusetts. In 1810 the Boston to Worcester route was straightened into an official turnpike (the present Route 9), and the steam train reached the center in 1824. The Massachusetts Turnpike (Interstate 90) and Interstate 495 now meet near the town, and a CSX rail freight yard sits close to that intersection.

The town lists eight entries on the National Register of Historic Places, among them the West Main Street Historic District, the Vintonville Historic District and the Westborough State Hospital. Historic buildings can limit exterior changes, which can affect where an outdoor unit may be placed. Homes from 1939 or earlier number 975 (11.4%), a smaller share than the 16.6% of the middle town.
## Electric utility and rebates

National Grid serves Westborough, according to its official Massachusetts Electric Company territory list, and it is a Mass Save sponsor. That means the Mass Save heat pump rebates apply, subject to the program terms. The details are on our [heat pump page](/cities/westborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is electric heat common in Westborough?
faq.a: Yes. Electricity heats 26.8% of occupied Westborough homes, the 3rd-highest share among the 50 towns we serve. If you have baseboard or an electric furnace, a heat pump is often worth pricing, because it can deliver the same heat using less electricity. Gas is still more common, at 48.5%, so check which fuel your building uses.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Westborough rental?
faq.a: Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord pays for heat under the State Sanitary Code, and rented homes must stay at least 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight in the heating season. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: Do Westborough apartment buildings need special equipment?
faq.a: Often they do. According to the ACS 2022, about 42.7% of Westborough homes are in multi-unit buildings, so shared boilers, rooftop units and individual ductless systems can all come into play. We assess the building and the heating load of each unit before we quote a system.

faq.q: Which utility serves Westborough, and does Mass Save apply?
faq.a: National Grid serves Westborough, and it sponsors Mass Save. The 2026 whole-home heat pump rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, if the home is sufficiently weatherized and an eligible installer does the work. Terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com. Partial-home rebates also exist, at $1,125 per ton.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 3,863 Westborough homes, electricity 2,133 and fuel oil 1,589, a three-way split that makes a failed heating plant a different job from one building to the next. Gas work also needs a permit and an inspection.
body: ## Three fuels, three kinds of replacement

Westborough does not lean on one fuel. Utility gas heats 3,863 occupied homes (48.5%), electricity heats 2,133 (26.8%) and fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,589 (20.0%). Bottled gas serves 187 homes and wood serves 102. A boiler or furnace call here starts with finding out which of those the building uses.
### Gas

The town ranks 22nd of 50 for utility gas, almost exactly in the middle. For a gas home the usual job is a like-for-like swap. The median home was built in 1976 and 2,643 homes date from 1960 to 1979, so it is worth asking for a heating-load figure rather than copying the old output.
### Oil

Oil ranks 44th of 50 here, with 1,589 homes. A household in that group can choose between new oil equipment, gas where a main passes the lot, or a heat pump. With fewer oil homes than in most MetroWest towns, nearby gas hookups are a fair question to ask.
### Electric heat

Electric heat is the Westborough story: 2,133 homes, the 3rd-highest share of the 50 towns. When an electric furnace or a run of baseboard heaters fails, a heat pump is often the first alternative to price, and the heat pump page covers it.
### Permits for gas work

A new gas furnace or boiler needs a permit from a licensed plumber or gas fitter and ends with a final inspection. Because Westborough has 3,651 homes in multi-unit buildings, the person ordering the work may be an owner, a board or a property manager, and the permit still follows the same route.
### Large buildings

There are 2,778 units in buildings of five or more (32.5%) and 426 in buildings of 3 to 4 units. Heating in those buildings can be central or unit by unit. Before a replacement, find out which one you have.
### Seasonal timing

A heating failure in January is an emergency, and we answer calls at (508) 786-8755 around the clock. Planning a replacement in the shoulder months leaves time to compare options. For upkeep that reduces breakdowns, see the [maintenance page](/cities/westborough/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Is gas or electricity the main heat in Westborough?
faq.a: Gas leads. Utility gas heats 48.5% of occupied Westborough homes and electricity heats 26.8%, with fuel oil at 20.0%. The mix is unusually balanced for the region, so a neighbor's replacement may not match yours. Ask what your own building uses before comparing quotes.

faq.q: Can a Westborough oil boiler be switched to gas?
faq.a: Only if a gas main reaches the property and the utility will connect it. If it does, the conversion is gas-fitter work with a permit and a final inspection. If it does not, the options are new oil equipment or a heat pump.

faq.q: What should I check before replacing a boiler in a multi-unit building?
faq.a: Find out whether the heat is central or unit by unit, and who owns the equipment. About one Westborough home in three sits in a building of five or more units. If the boiler is shared, the decision usually goes through the owner or board, and a heating-load assessment of the whole building comes first.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Westborough has 4,213 detached houses, 678 townhouses and 3,651 units in multi-unit buildings, so cooling ranges from one rooftop unit for a building to a single ductless head for an apartment. We match the system to the building.
body: ## One town, three kinds of cooling job

Single-family detached homes are only 49.3% of Westborough's 8,552 housing units, which ranks the town 48th of 50. The other half is mixed: 678 attached townhouses (7.9%), 447 units in two-unit buildings, 426 in buildings of 3 to 4 units, 2,778 in buildings of five or more, and 10 mobile homes.
### Detached houses

Where a forced-air furnace already has ducts, a central air conditioner can often share them if they are the right size. Many older houses were built without central air. In a house heated by hot-water baseboards, a ductless system or a small-duct system is the usual path.
### Apartments and condominiums

With 42.7% of homes in multi-unit buildings, the town ranks 3rd of 50, and the median of the 50 towns is 16.1%. Cooling in a large building may be a shared rooftop system, individual condensers on a pad or a ductless head in each apartment. Which one applies is often set by the building's owner or association, so ask them before ordering equipment.
### Renters and cooling
Cooling in a Westborough rental is a matter for the lease and the landlord. The 3,112 renter households should read the lease before adding any equipment.
### Electric homes and heat pumps

Since 2,133 homes already run on electricity, a heat pump can turn a cooling purchase into a heating upgrade. It cools in summer and heats in winter. The question is whether the home's heating load supports it, and that is something we assess first.
### Water, trees and placement

The town has 1.1 square miles of water, including Lake Chauncy and several ponds, and average elevation near 300 feet. Condenser placement should keep the unit clear of low, wet spots and let the drain run away from the foundation.
### Repair or replace

A unit that cools poorly may only need a coil cleaning or a part. Replacement becomes the better path when a compressor fails on aging equipment. We write both options down so you can compare. For all-season options, see the [heat pump page](/cities/westborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a Westborough apartment?
faq.a: Often, with a ductless mini-split or a through-wall unit, but the building decides. About 42.7% of town homes are in multi-unit buildings, and exterior equipment usually needs the owner's or association's approval. Ask before buying, and have a technician check the electrical capacity of the unit.

faq.q: Is a heat pump better than central air for a Westborough house?
faq.a: It can be, if you also want to replace heating. A heat pump both cools and heats, which matters when electricity already heats 26.8% of town homes. If your current heat is gas and works well, central air alone may be the simpler path. A load assessment helps decide.

faq.q: Does the older housing change how air conditioning is installed?
faq.a: It can. About 56.9% of Westborough homes date before 1980, and many older houses have no ducts. In those cases ductless heads or a small-duct system fits better than central air. A technician looks at attic access, wall space and the panel before suggesting a layout.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: National Grid serves Westborough, so the Mass Save heat pump path is open to qualifying homes. With 2,133 electric-heat homes, 1,589 on oil and 187 on bottled gas, many households have a reason to compare.
body: ## Westborough on National Grid

Westborough is on National Grid's territory list, so Mass Save rebates can apply to qualifying homes: $2,650 per ton up to $8,500 for a whole-home system in 2026. The rest of the rules are collected on our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Electric homes first

The 2,133 electric-heat homes are the clearest candidates. If the heat is baseboard or an electric furnace, a heat pump delivers the same warmth with less electricity. Westborough ranks 3rd of 50 for electric heat, against a middle-town share of 10.1%. The census does not say what type of electric heat each home has, so check your own.
### Oil and bottled gas

Fuel oil heats 1,589 homes and bottled gas 187. Both are delivered, so those households can price a cold-climate heat pump against another delivered-fuel boiler. A home keeping its boiler as a backup is a partial-home setup, with a smaller rebate than the whole-home one.
### Gas homes
With 3,863 homes on utility gas, many households have an efficient fuel already. For them a heat pump may fit best as an addition that also cools, or in a room that the furnace serves poorly.
### The weatherization test against local ages

A whole-home rebate needs the house to count as weatherized, and the simplest way is a build year of 2000 or later. In Westborough that covers 1,582 homes (18.5%), including 1,026 built since 2010. The other 2,106 homes from 1980 to 1999 and the 4,864 built before 1980 would need an assessment or earlier work first.
### Ducted or ductless by building type

Detached houses (4,213) with working ducts can take a ducted system. Ductless heads suit baseboard houses, additions and the 3,651 units in multi-unit buildings. In a large building the owner, not the tenant, normally approves the outdoor equipment.
### Sizing
We assess the home's heating load before quoting a system. For cooling questions, see the [air conditioning page](/cities/westborough/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Does Mass Save apply in Westborough?
faq.a: Yes, in general. National Grid serves the town and is a Mass Save sponsor, so qualifying homes can apply, subject to the program terms and a weatherization test. Confirm current rules at masssave.com, since terms can change, and check that your installer is an eligible one before signing anything.

faq.q: Should a Westborough home with electric baseboard get a heat pump?
faq.a: It is worth pricing. With 26.8% of town homes on electric heat, baseboard is common. A heat pump can deliver the same heat with less electricity and add cooling. Ductless heads fit baseboard houses because no ducts are needed, and the number of heads depends on the home's layout and load.

faq.q: Can I keep my oil boiler and add a heat pump in Westborough?
faq.a: Yes. A partial-home setup lets the heat pump do most of the work and the boiler cover the coldest days. About one home in five in town heats with oil, so the question is common. The rebate is smaller than for a whole-home system, and you still service the boiler.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Westborough has 4,850 owner households and 3,112 renter households, with gas, electric, oil and bottled gas all in use. Upkeep depends on the fuel and on who owns the equipment, so we ask both questions first.
body: ## Upkeep by fuel and by owner
Owners occupy 4,850 Westborough households (60.9%) and renters occupy 3,112 (39.1%). The fuel mix is also varied, so no single checklist fits every address.
### Gas, 3,863 homes
A gas check looks at the burner, the heat exchanger, the venting and the controls, and includes carbon monoxide testing. It is the visit that catches the safety problems.
### Electric, 2,133 homes

An electric home with a heat pump needs coil cleaning, filter changes and a look at the outdoor unit. A home with baseboard or an electric furnace has less to service, but the thermostats, wiring and fans still deserve a look.
### Oil, 1,589 homes
An oil system needs a cleaning each year. The technician cleans the burner and boiler or furnace and checks combustion. Doing it before the season avoids a failure on the first cold night.
### Bottled gas, 187 homes
The same as gas, with an added look at the tank and regulator.
### Rental and multi-unit buildings

Westborough ranks 4th of 50 for renter households. A landlord or property manager with several units can book all the equipment in one pass before the season. Where each apartment has its own system, each one needs its own filter and coil care. Westborough counts 2,778 units in buildings of five or more, which is a lot of equipment to keep track of.
### Vacant units
The town has 590 vacant units. Equipment in an empty unit still needs a check before it is switched back to normal use.
### Seasonal schedule
Heating checks fit best from late summer through early autumn. Cooling and mini-split checks fit spring. Odd noises, smells and short cycling are signs to call at any time.
### Before the visit

Have the fuel type, the unit's age, its make and model and a note of what changed. A photo of the nameplate saves a step. For replacement, see the [heating page](/cities/westborough/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often does a Westborough oil system need servicing?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season. With 20.0% of homes using oil, many households fall into this group. Annual cleaning removes soot, lets the technician test combustion and finds worn parts before a cold snap turns them into a no-heat call.

faq.q: Do electric and heat pump homes in Westborough need maintenance?
faq.a: Yes, though less than combustion systems. Filters need regular changes, outdoor coils need to be clear of debris, and the refrigerant side should be checked. With 2,133 homes on electricity, including heat pumps, this is a common visit. Each indoor head of a mini-split has its own filter.

faq.q: Who arranges maintenance in a Westborough apartment building?
faq.a: It depends on who owns the equipment. For shared boilers or rooftop units, the owner, board or property manager arranges the service. For in-unit systems, the tenant or the landlord does, depending on the lease. Ask early, because with 39.1% of households renting, responsibility is worth clarifying.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Westborough has 975 homes from 1939 or earlier and 1,026 built since 2010, with 4,864 built before 1980. Older and newer homes face different air-quality questions, and so do the 3,651 units in multi-unit buildings.
body: ## Old, new and shared walls

The ACS 2022 divides Westborough's 8,552 housing units into bands: 975 from 1939 or earlier (11.4%), 1,246 from 1940 to 1959, 2,643 from 1960 to 1979, 2,106 from 1980 to 1999 and 1,582 from 2000 on. Of the newest group, 1,026 were built since 2010.
### Older houses

Houses built before 1980 are often leaky enough to ventilate themselves, which brings in outdoor dust and pollen along with fresh air. Westborough ranks 28th of 50 for that group, with 56.9% of homes. Before heavy renovation in a very old building, ask a qualified specialist about testing the old materials first.
### Newer houses

Westborough ranks 10th of 50 for homes built since 2010, which makes tightness a live question for more of its houses than in most MetroWest towns, since the middle town has 8.4%. A recent house is usually tight, so cooking fumes, moisture and furnishing chemicals stay inside unless a fan or ventilation system moves them out. Bath fans and range hoods vented outdoors matter most, and filters that are changed on time keep the air handler moving air as designed.
### Apartment and condominium buildings

Westborough ranks 3rd of 50 for homes in multi-unit buildings (42.7%). Smoke, cooking odors and moisture can move between units, and common ducts can carry them. Air sealing, balanced ventilation and a good filter in each unit are the realistic tools.
### Lakes, ponds and humidity

With 5.09 percent of its area in water and numerous ponds, Westborough has plenty of surface water. Basement dampness has its own causes, such as groundwater, plumbing or warm summer air meeting cool masonry. Treat the source first and use a dehumidifier for the air.
### Ducts and filters

Duct cleaning is a narrow remedy for visible mold, heavy dirt or renovation dust. Most households do better with the filter on schedule and a look at airflow. See the [maintenance page](/cities/westborough/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: What should Westborough apartment dwellers know about air quality?
faq.a: Shared walls and shared ducts let cooking fumes, smoke and moisture travel. With 42.7% of homes in multi-unit buildings, this is a common issue. Sealing gaps, running bath and kitchen fans, and keeping a clean filter in your own unit help. Ask the owner about shared ventilation.

faq.q: Do newer Westborough homes need ventilation help?
faq.a: Often. A house built in 2000 or later is usually tight, and the town has 1,582 of them. Moisture, cooking fumes and chemicals from furnishings stay indoors unless ventilation moves them out. Check that fans run and vent outdoors. If the air still feels stale after that, ask about adding a fresh-air path to the system. Opening a window on a mild day is a quick test of whether stale air is the problem.

faq.q: Is duct cleaning worth it in a Westborough house?
faq.a: Only in specific cases: ducts with visible mold, heavy dirt or debris from renovation. Otherwise a better filter on schedule and a look at airflow are the first steps. We inspect the ducts and the filter and say what we would do, rather than selling cleaning by default.
